title: Tiered emergency response and reporting
summary: We operate three response levels based on incident severity, with defined activation triggers, reporting timelines, and responsible organizations.

content.overview: We classify emergencies into three levels to ensure proportional resource mobilization and timely escalation. Level I (fatality or ≥3 severe injuries) triggers immediate company-wide response and external notification within 30 minutes; Level II (severe injury or major equipment loss ≥500k RMB) triggers project-level response and report to company within 2 hours; Level III (minor injury or general equipment failure) is handled locally and reported within 24 hours.
content.details: This triage prevents over-escalation for minor incidents while ensuring serious events receive senior management and regulatory attention quickly. Thresholds: Level I activates for any fatality or three or more severe injuries (inpatient cases), Level II for a single severe injury or asset damage ≥500k RMB, Level III for others. We chose 30-minute reporting to authorities and parent company for Level I to align with mandatory governmental timelines. The 2-hour window for Level II gives project teams time to stabilize the scene and gather initial facts without delay.
content.examples: Scenario A: one worker hospitalized with a fracture → Level II, project HSE manager activates site emergency plan, notifies company HSE within 2 hours. Scenario B: fatality → Level I, company crisis cell activated, call to local emergency bureau within 30 min.
content.references: Company emergency response plan, applicable regulations.
content.caveats: Incident severity classification must be confirmed quickly; initial reports may be preliminary. Delays in classification can cause inappropriate response levels. Financial loss threshold should be consistently assessed.
